research_progress.source_confidence_semantics: Heuristic research-source confidence only: direct official GOV.UK, Natural England, Defra, Planning Data and National Data Library verification; 2026 currentness where available; ALC/BMV strategic-vs-detailed mapping, soil evidence, planning consultation, agricultural EIA screening/consent, agricultural tenancy and agricultural permitted-development/prior-approval separation. Not parcel-level agricultural land, soil, tenancy or planning accuracy.

verification.method: Direct official-web verification plus repository duplicate searches

official_sources.name: Planning Data agricultural land classification dataset
official_sources.fact: Planning Data exposes 585 ALC records from one provider and states its current origin is MHCLG pending authoritative replacement.
official_sources.gate: Planning Data ALC is discovery/provenance data and must not be treated as complete authoritative parcel grading.

official_sources.name: Natural England post-1988 ALC polygons
official_sources.fact: Natural England publishes post-1988 ALC survey polygons with grade and survey-job information; dataset updated 19 June 2026.
official_sources.gate: Survey polygons only cover surveyed areas and do not prove a current detailed grade for unsurveyed or differently bounded land.

official_sources.name: Predictive Agricultural Land Classification Map for England
official_sources.fact: Defra's predictive ALC map, updated 1 July 2026, gives a strategic 1:250,000 national view and subdivides grade 3.
official_sources.gate: Predictive strategic mapping is not a substitute for a detailed site survey or exact parcel grade.

official_sources.name: Provisional Agricultural Land Classification
official_sources.fact: Natural England's provisional ALC was digitised from historic 1:250,000 reconnaissance mapping.
official_sources.gate: Provisional mapping is strategic legacy evidence and must not be promoted to detailed 3a/3b parcel truth.

official_sources.name: Planning practice guidance: Natural environment
official_sources.fact: Planning guidance defines BMV land as grades 1, 2 and 3a and requires planning decisions to consider its economic and other benefits.
official_sources.gate: BMV policy weight is not an automatic refusal and map presence alone is not a parcel decision.

official_sources.name: Land Use Framework
official_sources.fact: England's first Land Use Framework was published in March 2026 and links future land-use decisions with food, housing, infrastructure and nature.
official_sources.gate: National framework analysis is not a planning allocation, consent or exact parcel development conclusion.

official_sources.name: Land Use Framework accessible version
official_sources.fact: The accessible 2026 framework sets out better land-use decision making and implementation principles.
official_sources.gate: Framework principles do not override local plans, statutory consents or site-specific evidence.

official_sources.name: Planning Data BMV agricultural land consideration
official_sources.fact: Planning Data records BMV as a planning consideration but marks the design stage as backlog with unknown expected record count and update frequency.
official_sources.gate: A backlog schema must not be interpreted as a complete BMV national dataset or no-constraint result.

official_sources.name: Planning Data ALC screen
official_sources.fact: Planning Data describes ALC as a planning consideration used to assess farmland quality and records the Natural England consultation trigger context.
official_sources.gate: Design-stage research is not legislation, authoritative survey evidence or a parcel grade.

official_sources.name: Natural England agricultural land development assessment publication
official_sources.fact: Natural England publishes guidance for LPAs and developers assessing development proposals affecting agricultural land.
official_sources.gate: Guidance identifies evidence requirements but does not determine an individual application.

official_sources.name: Guide to assessing development proposals on agricultural land
official_sources.fact: The guide explains ALC use and the Natural England consultation trigger for certain non-agricultural development involving 20ha or more of BMV land outside the development plan.
official_sources.gate: A consultation trigger is not a refusal, and absence of detailed data can require a new site survey rather than a no-BMV conclusion.

official_sources.name: NPPF Chapter 15 natural environment
official_sources.fact: NPPF Chapter 15 requires policies and decisions to protect soils and recognise the benefits of BMV agricultural land.
official_sources.gate: National policy is a decision input, not parcel-specific permission or measured land quality.

official_sources.name: Construction soil code of practice
official_sources.fact: Defra retains its construction soil code as practical advice but explicitly notes it has not been updated to reflect all current controls.
official_sources.gate: The code is guidance and its legacy status must not be treated as current legal compliance or site-specific soil quality.

official_sources.name: Indicators of Soil Health for England 2026
official_sources.fact: The March 2026 official statistics provide interim national-scale soil-health indicators for rural England.
official_sources.gate: National soil-health indicators are not a parcel soil survey or development suitability score.

official_sources.name: Developers environmental advice on planning proposals
official_sources.fact: GOV.UK directs developers to Natural England advice where proposals affect BMV agricultural land.
official_sources.gate: Seeking advice does not imply objection, permission or an exact land grade.

official_sources.name: NSIP public bodies advice Annex C Natural England
official_sources.fact: NSIP advice states that where significant agricultural development is necessary, poorer-quality land should be preferred to higher-quality land and soils protected during development.
official_sources.gate: NSIP advice is process guidance and not a parcel-specific DCO outcome or ALC survey.

official_sources.name: Agricultural tenancies guidance
official_sources.fact: Defra guidance distinguishes Farm Business Tenancies from Agricultural Holdings Act 1986 tenancies and explains security, compensation and termination routes.
official_sources.gate: Agricultural ownership or mapped farming use does not prove vacant possession, tenancy terms or ability to develop.

official_sources.name: Planning practice guidance: when permission is required
official_sources.fact: Planning guidance explains agricultural Class Q and agricultural permitted-development concepts, including prior-approval requirements.
official_sources.gate: Some PPG text can lag later GPDO amendments; exact current Class Q/R/A/B limits must be checked against current law and live application requirements.

official_sources.name: Planning Data Class Q agricultural buildings to dwellinghouses
official_sources.fact: Planning Data records Class Q as an authoritative permitted-development-right category for agricultural buildings to dwellinghouses.
official_sources.gate: A category record does not prove a building qualifies, prior approval is granted or current numerical limits are satisfied.

official_sources.name: Planning Data Class R agricultural buildings flexible commercial use
official_sources.fact: Planning Data records Class R as an agricultural-building flexible-use permitted-development category.
official_sources.gate: Entity metadata may retain historic use-class wording; current scope and limits require current GPDO evidence and site eligibility.

official_sources.name: Planning Data Class S agricultural buildings to state-funded school
official_sources.fact: Planning Data records Class S for change of agricultural buildings to state-funded school use.
official_sources.gate: The PDR category does not prove prior approval, lawful agricultural use or site eligibility.

official_sources.name: Planning Data permitted-development-right dataset editor
official_sources.fact: The Planning Data editor lists multiple PDR categories including Q, R and S with documentation links and metadata.
official_sources.gate: Dataset-editor metadata is a discovery layer; stale descriptions must not override current legislation.

official_sources.name: Defra farming blog: changes to permitted development rights
official_sources.fact: Defra's farming service explains that changes effective 21 May 2024 amended four PDRs supporting agricultural development and reuse of agricultural buildings.
official_sources.gate: A summary blog is not a substitute for checking current GPDO conditions, exclusions and prior-approval requirements.

official_sources.name: Consultation on PDR flexibilities for agriculture and rural diversification
official_sources.fact: The consultation documented proposals around Class R and Part 6 agricultural rights and wider farm diversification.
official_sources.gate: Consultation proposals are not current rights unless implemented in legislation.

official_sources.name: Technical consultation on consequential PDR changes
official_sources.fact: The technical consultation documented proposed changes to agricultural-building PDR categories following use-class reforms.
official_sources.gate: Proposed amendments are not final law and must not be used as current permission evidence.

official_sources.name: Technical consultation outcome on consequential PDR changes
official_sources.fact: The consultation outcome records which proposed agricultural-building PDR changes government took forward.
official_sources.gate: A consultation outcome still requires the operative GPDO text and site-specific conditions to determine lawful development.

official_sources.name: Changing uncultivated semi-natural and rural land
official_sources.fact: Natural England and Defra guidance, updated 12 May 2026, explains EIA Agriculture controls for productivity changes and restructuring rural land.
official_sources.gate: Agricultural use does not exempt land-change projects from EIA Agriculture screening or consent requirements.

official_sources.name: Check if an EIA Agriculture screening decision is needed
official_sources.fact: The May 2026 guidance explains when uncultivated, semi-natural or rural restructuring projects require a Natural England screening decision.
official_sources.gate: Screening requirement is not consent, and a screening notice/result must not be inferred from land cover alone.

official_sources.name: Apply for an EIA Agriculture screening decision
official_sources.fact: Applying for screening is the first step of a potentially two-step EIA Agriculture process.
official_sources.gate: Application submission is not a positive screening decision or permission to start work.

official_sources.name: Apply for an EIA Agriculture consent decision
official_sources.fact: Where screening identifies likely significant effects, a consent decision can be required as the second stage.
official_sources.gate: Screening and consent are distinct stages; neither planning status nor agricultural ownership proves consent.

official_sources.name: EIA Agriculture public register
official_sources.fact: Natural England's register, updated 1 July 2026, lists screening and consent decisions and current consent consultations.
official_sources.gate: A register search needs exact project/location matching; no hit must not automatically be treated as no EIA requirement.

official_sources.name: EIA1a rural restructuring screening form
official_sources.fact: EIA1a covers rural-land restructuring and publishes thresholds for field-boundary and earth-moving projects.
official_sources.gate: Threshold exceedance triggers screening analysis, not automatic refusal or consent.

official_sources.name: EIA1 uncultivated or semi-natural land screening form
official_sources.fact: EIA1 applies to projects increasing agricultural productivity on 2ha or more of uncultivated land or semi-natural areas.
official_sources.gate: Area threshold and land status require evidence; mapped agriculture alone does not decide screening outcome.

official_sources.name: EIA Agriculture consent and scoping forms
official_sources.fact: Natural England publishes EIA4 consent and EIA3 scoping forms for projects requiring the second-stage process.
official_sources.gate: A form or scoping opinion is not consent to carry out the project.

official_sources.name: EIA Agriculture inspection guidance
official_sources.fact: Natural England may inspect land for screening applications or suspected unapproved activity and issues the decision separately from the inspector's recommendation.
official_sources.gate: Inspection or recommendation is not the final screening or enforcement outcome.

official_sources.name: Natural England environmental enforcement laws
official_sources.fact: Natural England lists EIA Agriculture breaches among its environmental enforcement responsibilities.
official_sources.gate: A suspected breach or complaint is not proof of an offence, stop notice or remediation order.

official_sources.name: Farming Rules for Water
official_sources.fact: England's Farming Rules for Water require precautions against agricultural diffuse pollution and soil erosion.
official_sources.gate: Compliance duties for farming operations are not planning permission or a parcel development prohibition.

official_sources.name: Post-1988 ALC survey ALCR12891
official_sources.fact: Natural England publishes a detailed historic post-1988 ALC survey record with site mapping and survey-report provenance; metadata updated 13 July 2026.
official_sources.gate: A detailed survey is authoritative for its surveyed site/date, not for unrelated parcels or later physical changes.

official_sources.name: Post-1988 ALC survey ALCR13695
official_sources.fact: Natural England's ALCR13695 record documents detailed historic ALC survey material and grade-3 subdivision capability; metadata updated 13 July 2026.
official_sources.gate: Survey scale and boundary must be matched exactly before using grades for a target site.

official_sources.name: Post-1988 ALC survey ALCR18694
official_sources.fact: Natural England publishes ALCR18694 as a detailed post-1988 survey record with map/report provenance; metadata updated 13 July 2026.
official_sources.gate: Historic detailed survey evidence must not be spatially generalized outside the actual surveyed area.

official_sources.name: Post-1988 ALC survey ALCR19394
official_sources.fact: ALCR19394 is a Natural England site-specific detailed ALC survey record with grade 3a/3b detail where mapped.
official_sources.gate: Site-specific survey data cannot be transferred to neighbouring or similarly named land without geometry match.

official_sources.name: Post-1988 ALC survey ALCL04594
official_sources.fact: ALCL04594 records a detailed Natural England ALC survey and notes that soil sample-point and pit descriptions may be available for some surveys.
official_sources.gate: Availability of sample-point evidence does not prove coverage of every part of a target parcel.

official_sources.name: Post-1988 ALC survey ALCR16094
official_sources.fact: ALCR16094 is a detailed Natural England survey where mapped grade 3 can include 3a/3b subdivision.
official_sources.gate: Grade 3 on a strategic map must not be assumed to be 3a or 3b without detailed evidence.

official_sources.name: Post-1988 ALC survey ALCR00691a
official_sources.fact: ALCR00691a is a historic detailed ALC survey record using the post-1988 methodology.
official_sources.gate: Historic survey date and present land condition must be separated; the record is not a live physical-condition survey.

official_sources.name: Post-1988 ALC survey ALCL04596
official_sources.fact: ALCL04596 provides detailed site survey provenance and mapping at site-specific scales.
official_sources.gate: Survey job identity and polygon boundary must be matched before parcel attribution.

official_sources.name: Post-1988 ALC survey ALCR09497
official_sources.fact: ALCR09497 documents a detailed post-1988 Natural England survey prepared for a specific local-plan site context.
official_sources.gate: Local-plan survey context is not current planning allocation, permission or evidence for other parcels.
